svg.title: Build the Acquisition System in 30 Days
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-land-desk-launch; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Build the Acquisition System in 30 Days; subtitle: Four weekly deliverables; first-deal timing remains 3–12 months; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values are cumulative milestone days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. This sprint establishes operating readiness and a measured pipeline, not a promised closing. Canonical annual scenarios are Conservative: $200,000 gross × 12% = $24,000 owner net with 1 FT + 3 C; Base-Case: $850,000 gross × 18.5% = $157,250 owner net with 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled Small-Team: $1,500,000 gross × 25% = $375,000 owner net with 2 FT + 4 C.; caption: Advance by completed evidence and funded obligations. Illiquidity, absent legal access, and environmental constraints can defeat attractive headline spreads before the first resale.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Select market and capital limits; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one county and parcel thesis, assemble recorded sale comparables, and document zoning and subdivision contacts. Set maximum cash exposure per parcel, minimum operating runway, and the four startup capital allocations before soliciting sellers.; label: Days 8-14; value: Build the screening evidence chain; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure QGIS parcel layers, assessor-record imports, comparable-sale tracking, and a parcel evidence checklist. Screen an initial 250 unique parcels and manually inspect 25 records for mapping, ownership, and sale-comparison errors before increasing throughput.; label: Days 15-21; value: Test outreach and transaction support; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Contact a measured subset of qualified owners and record parcel-level responses rather than message counts. Obtain title-provider terms, survey quotes, and specialist availability; prepare written offer forms and jurisdiction-specific disclosure checklists.; label: Days 22-30; value: Review offers and funded runway; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Underwrite responsive opportunities, issue only offers supported by evidence, and schedule inspection deadlines. Reconcile funnel counts, committed cash, remaining runway, and open defects; carry incomplete investigations forward without treating unsigned or unclosed deals as revenue.

text.title: Build the Acquisition System in 30 Days
text.tspan: Build the Acquisition System in 30 Days

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Select market and capital limits; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one county and parcel thesis, assemble recorded sale comparables, and document zoning and subdivision contacts. Set maximum cash exposure per parcel, minimum operating runway, and the four startup capital allocations before soliciting sellers.

label: Days 8-14; value: Build the screening evidence chain; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure QGIS parcel layers, assessor-record imports, comparable-sale tracking, and a parcel evidence checklist. Screen an initial 250 unique parcels and manually inspect 25 records for mapping, ownership, and sale-comparison errors before increasing throughput.

label: Days 15-21; value: Test outreach and transaction support; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Contact a measured subset of qualified owners and record parcel-level responses rather than message counts. Obtain title-provider terms, survey quotes, and specialist availability; prepare written offer forms and jurisdiction-specific disclosure checklists.

label: Days 22-30; value: Review offers and funded runway; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Underwrite responsive opportunities, issue only offers supported by evidence, and schedule inspection deadlines. Reconcile funnel counts, committed cash, remaining runway, and open defects; carry incomplete investigations forward without treating unsigned or unclosed deals as revenue.

text.title: Assumptions: Numeric values are cumulative milestone days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. This sprint establishes operating readiness and a measured pipeline, not a promised closing. Canonical annual scenarios are Conservative: $200,000 gross × 12% = $24,000 owner net with 1 FT + 3 C; Base-Case: $850,000 gross × 18.5% = $157,250 owner net with 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled Small-Team: $1,500,000 gross × 25% = $375,000 owner net with 2 FT + 4 C.
